title: Hybridization of RNA Probes
author: Jonathan Houseley
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bns4megw
materials: Prehybridize for 01:00:00 at 65 °C with 7.5 mL, ULTRAHyb . This is an important step so do not feel tempted to skip it or shorten it. It allows blocking agents in the hybridization buffer to occupy nonspecific binding sites. In our hands, 65 °C is the best temperature for almost all RNA probes. However, if cross-hybridization to ribosomal RNA is observed, increase the prehybridization, hybridization, and washing temperatures to 68 °C. Beware that this is often caused by the oven temperature calibration drifting such that the oven is not actually at the set temperature of 65 °C. Leave a beaker of water overnight in the oven and check the temperature with a trustworthy thermometer to be sure. In contrast, if the probe is unavoidably AT rich (such as the probe used in Fig. 2d ) and a very low signal is obtained, reduce the prehybridization, hybridization and washing temperature to 60 °C and hybridize again with the same probe. Further temperature optimization is unlikely to improve the signal.

To make the probe, mix the following reagents in the given order at Room temperature in a 1.5 mL screw cap tube: 5 µL, gel purified template (the absolute amount does not seem to be critical). 0.6 µL, 100 μM rUTP 3.7 µL, milliQ H2O 1 µL, 10 mM rCTP/rGTP/rATP 2 µL, 100 mM DTT 0.2 µL, 10 mg/mL BSA 4 µL, 5× transcription buffer 2.5 µL 3000 Ci/mMol [α -32 P] rUTP 1 µL, T7 RNA polymerase Some cold UTP is important otherwise the in vitro transcription is inefficient. However, more cold UTP means that the radioactivity per probe molecule is lower, reducing the signal. This amount is a compromise, try not to change unless absolutely necessary. It is critical that the polymerase is added after the radioactive rUTP, then mixed well.
Wrap the membrane in Saran Wrap.

steps.title: Inspect hybridization bottles
steps.instruction: Verify that hybridization bottles and internal seals are intact to prevent radioactive buffer leaks.

steps.title: Prewarm ULTRAHyb buffer
steps.instruction: Place a bottle of ULTRAHyb in a water bath and prewarm to 68 °C until the SDS fully dissolves (approximately 15–20 min).

steps.title: Prepare membrane for hybridization
steps.instruction: Wet the membrane with 0.1× SSC containing 0.1 % SDS, roll it RNA‑face inward, drop into the hybridization bottle, slowly rotate to unroll against the bottle wall, use a Stripette to assist, remove air bubbles, and place the bottle in the hybridization oven ensuring the membrane edge moves with rotation; balance bottles including liquid volume; optionally place two membranes per bottle (one glass‑facing, one interior).

steps.title: Label probe (incubation)
steps.instruction: Mix labeling components, then incubate at 37 °C for 1–2 h (01:00:00–02:00:00); longer incubations (≥2 h) are acceptable.

steps.title: Prepare Quick Spin column
steps.instruction: Flick the mini Quick Spin column inverted then right‑side up to settle the sepharose at the bottom, remove the top and bottom caps as per product instructions.

steps.title: Centrifuge column into tube
steps.instruction: Place the column in a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, spin at 1000 × g for 30 s (room temperature), discard the tube, then transfer the column into a new 1.5 mL screw‑cap tube.

steps.title: Load probe onto sepharose
steps.instruction: Dilute the probe with water to a final volume of 50 µL and carefully pipette onto the centre of the sepharose matrix in the column.

steps.title: Bind probe to column
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at 1000 × g for 4 min (room temperature) to allow probe binding.

steps.title: Test radioactive incorporation
steps.instruction: Hold the probe‑loaded column and a free probe at equal distances from a Geiger counter using tweezers; ensure the counter reads comparable signals (≥50 % label incorporated). Discard the column to radioactive waste.

steps.title: Add probe to hybridization bottle
steps.instruction: While holding the bottle vertically, add the probe so it falls directly into the hybridization buffer, then rotate the bottle at 65 °C overnight.

steps.title: Store and reuse probe
steps.instruction: Transfer the probe to a 50 mL Falcon tube and store at –20 °C. RNA and oligonucleotide probes may be reused up to two times (three total uses) within one to two weeks, considering isotope half‑life. To reuse, pre‑hybridize the membrane with half the normal hybridization buffer, defrost the probe in a beaker of hot water for 20 min, then add it to the hybridization bottle.

steps.title: Low‑stringency washes (6× SSC)
steps.instruction: Pour ~50 mL of 6× SSC into the bottle, close tightly, shake gently, then discard the wash; repeat this wash a second time.

steps.title: Incubate with 6× SSC
steps.instruction: Add 50 mL of 6× SSC, place the bottle back in the hybridization oven, rotate at 65 °C for at least 20 min, and balance the bottle with another containing 50 mL liquid.

steps.title: High‑stringency washes (0.1× SSC, 0.1% SDS)
steps.instruction: Discard the 6× SSC, add 50 mL of pre‑warmed (65 °C) 0.1× SSC with 0.1 % SDS, rotate at 65 °C for 20 min; repeat this wash 2–3 times.

steps.title: Remove membrane and clean bottle
steps.instruction: Pour off the final wash, use tweezers to lift the membrane onto a paper towel, then rinse the bottle with water and wipe dry; clean the lid by running water through it and wiping the interior, avoiding removal of the rubber seal, and treat the lid as contaminated.

steps.title: Pat membrane semi‑dry
steps.instruction: Gently pat the membrane to a semi‑dry state behind a Perspex shield to protect against radioactivity.

steps.title: Assess signal with Geiger counter
steps.instruction: Measure the membrane signal with a Geiger counter to estimate exposure time; if adjustment is needed, blank and re‑expose the phosphor screen. For very intense signals (thousands of counts s⁻¹), expose the screen to natural UV light for several days (e.g., on a windowsill). Example guideline: 400 cps → 2 h exposure for good quality.

steps.title: Expose membrane to phosphor screen
steps.instruction: Place the membrane in a cassette with a storage phosphor screen; ensure the screen is blanked just before use as it slowly re‑exposes over time.
